blurb: An ordinary string literal, `"…"`, closes on the line it opens on. This one reaches the end of the line with no closing `"`, so the lexer reports it at the opening quote and skips the rest of the line. Add the closing quote. For a line break in the value write `\n`, or use a multi-line string literal.
example:
const Greeting: String = "hello      // ✗ no closing quote
const Greeting: String = "hello"   // ✓
summary: A string literal is not terminated.
